The Context Window, Live

One agent task, 40 turns, one context window. Press play and watch the window fill with tool results and history until it overflows. Then switch on the fixes one at a time (lean tools and skills, tool result clearing, compaction, sub-agents, prompt caching) and see what each does to the window, the total tokens and the bill.

Turn 0 of 40
Window now0
Peak window0
Input tokens so far0
Cost so far$0
Events—

A toy model, not a benchmark. Assumptions: system prompt 1,500 tokens, tools 12,000 (lean: 2,500 with deferred definitions and skill metadata), project file 3,000; each turn adds 300 tokens of model text and a 2,500-token tool result; clearing keeps the last 3 results; compaction at 60% of the window leaves a 2,000-token summary; sub-agents take every 10th block of work and return 1,500 tokens (their own tokens are not counted; Anthropic reports multi-agent systems use about 15× the tokens of chat); price example $3 per million input tokens, caching with 1.25× writes and 0.1× reads as in Claude’s docs. Read the series: Part 1 · what goes in · long tasks · caching and measuring.

Disclosure: Claude, made by Anthropic, helps write this site, and many of the techniques shown come from Anthropic’s posts and docs.
